rows.question: In the grand tapestry of Wyoming's cities, which city stands as the most populous, classified under the realms of 'High Population' or 'Low Population', while sharing whispers through the fences with the neighboring land of Colorado?
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_name,
  c.population,
  CASE WHEN c.population >= med.median_population THEN 'High Population' ELSE 'Low Population' END AS classification
FROM city c
JOIN border_info b ON b.state_name = c.state_name AND b.border = 'Colorado'
JOIN (
  SELECT
    'Wyoming' AS state_name,
    CASE
      WHEN (cnt % 2) = 1 THEN
        (SELECT population FROM city c2 WHERE c2.state_name = 'Wyoming' ORDER BY population DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET (cnt/2))
      ELSE
        (
          (SELECT population FROM city c3 WHERE c3.state_name = 'Wyoming' ORDER BY population DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET (cnt/2 - 1))
          +
          (SELECT population FROM city c4 WHERE c4.state_name = 'Wyoming' ORDER BY population DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET (cnt/2))
        ) / 2.0
    END AS median_population
  FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM city WHERE state_name = 'Wyoming')
) med ON med.state_name = c.state_name
WHERE c.state_name = 'Wyoming'
ORDER BY c.population DESC
LIMIT 1

SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.title,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pd.datasetId) AS dataset_count
FROM paper p
JOIN paperDataset pd ON p.paperId = pd.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId, p.title
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pd.datasetId) > 1
ORDER BY dataset_count DESC, p.paperId ASC

rows.question: What is the average number of companions on the scholarly voyage for each paper where Peter Mertens is the captain, but not counted among his crew?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH papers_with_pm AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.paperId
  FROM writes w
  JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
  JOIN paper p ON w.paperId = p.paperId
  WHERE a.authorName = 'Peter Mertens'
),
paper_author_counts AS (
  SELECT
    w.paperId,
    COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS total_authors
  FROM writes w
  WHERE w.paperId IN (SELECT paperId FROM papers_with_pm)
  GROUP BY w.paperId
)
SELECT AVG(total_authors - 1.0) AS average_coauthors
FROM paper_author_counts

  FROM paper p
  JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
  JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

rows.question: Which research work does Peter Mertens and Dina Barbian collaboratively contribute to, that started gaining attention after the millennium, and how significant is their impact in the scholarly environment?
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  p.title,
  p.year,
  p.numCitedBy,
  CASE
    WHEN p.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'Less Cited'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 100 THEN 'Highly Cited'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 25 THEN 'Moderately Cited'
    ELSE 'Less Cited'
  END AS impact_label
FROM paper p
JOIN writes w1 ON w1.paperId = p.paperId
JOIN author a1 ON a1.authorId = w1.authorId AND a1.authorName = 'Peter Mertens'
JOIN writes w2 ON w2.paperId = p.paperId
JOIN author a2 ON a2.authorId = w2.authorId AND a2.authorName = 'Dina Barbian'
WHERE p.year >= 2001
ORDER BY p.year ASC

rows.question: Could you please collect information on all the departments whose names start with 'M', have a budget greater than both zero and the average budget of all departments? Make sure the department details include their name and building, and only provide information about the instructor with the highest salary in each department, noting the instructor's ID, name, and salary. Also, categorize the department names as either "Long Name" or "Short Name" based on whether their length is greater than 10 characters.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH dept_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(budget) AS avg_budget FROM department
),
filtered_depts AS (
  SELECT dept_name, building, budget
  FROM department
  WHERE dept_name LIKE 'M%'
    AND budget > 0
    AND budget > (SELECT avg_budget FROM dept_avg)
),
max_salary_per_dept AS (
  SELECT dept_name, MAX(salary) AS max_salary
  FROM instructor
  GROUP BY dept_name
),
top_instructors AS (
  SELECT i.ID, i.name, i.dept_name, i.salary
  FROM instructor i
  JOIN max_salary_per_dept m
    ON i.dept_name = m.dept_name
   AND i.salary = m.max_salary
),
top_instructor_tiebreak AS (
  SELECT t.dept_name, MIN(t.ID) AS ID
  FROM top_instructors t
  GROUP BY t.dept_name
)
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  i.ID AS instructor_ID,
  i.name AS instructor_name,
  i.salary AS instructor_salary,
  CASE WHEN LENGTH(d.dept_name) > 10 THEN 'Long Name' ELSE 'Short Name' END AS name_length_category
FROM filtered_depts d
LEFT JOIN top_instructor_tiebreak tb
  ON tb.dept_name = d.dept_name
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON i.dept_name = d.dept_name
 AND i.ID = tb.ID
ORDER BY d.dept_name ASC

rows.question: Buildings with classrooms having an average capacity between 50 and 100, what is their average department budget?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH dept_budget_by_building AS (
  SELECT
    building,
    AVG(budget) AS dept_avg_budget
  FROM department
  GROUP BY building
),
classroom_by_building AS (
  SELECT
    building,
    AVG(capacity) AS avg_classroom_capacity
  FROM classroom
  GROUP BY building
)
SELECT
  cb.building,
  cb.avg_classroom_capacity,
  dbb.dept_avg_budget,
  AVG(dbb.dept_avg_budget) OVER () AS overall_avg_dept_budget
FROM classroom_by_building cb
JOIN dept_budget_by_building dbb
  ON cb.building = dbb.building
WHERE cb.avg_classroom_capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 100
ORDER BY cb.building

rows.question: In the realm where academic pursuits intertwine with fiscal prowess, what is the count of unique realms (departments) that navigate budgets beyond $100,000 and offer courses that soar above the basic tier of 2 credits, categorized by budget strata of opulence, moderation, and frugality?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH depts_with_qualifying_course AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.dept_name
  FROM department d
  JOIN course c ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
  WHERE c.credits > 2
    AND d.budget IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN d.budget > 100000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN d.budget > 50000 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS category,
  COUNT(*) AS dept_count
FROM department d
JOIN depts_with_qualifying_course q ON q.dept_name = d.dept_name
GROUP BY
  CASE
    WHEN d.budget > 100000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN d.budget > 50000 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END
ORDER BY CASE
  WHEN category = 'High' THEN 1
  WHEN category = 'Medium' THEN 2
  WHEN category = 'Low' THEN 3
END

rows.question: What is the average capacity of classrooms associated with each department for courses that do not have any prerequisites?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH classroom_core AS (
  SELECT building, room_number, capacity
  FROM classroom
),
courses_without_prereqs AS (
  SELECT c.course_id, c.dept_name
  FROM course c
  LEFT JOIN prereq p ON c.course_id = p.course_id
  WHERE p.course_id IS NULL
),
section_classroom_usage AS (
  SELECT s.course_id, s.building, s.room_number, cr.capacity
  FROM section s
  JOIN classroom_core cr ON s.building = cr.building AND s.room_number = cr.room_number
)
SELECT
  cwp.dept_name AS dept_name,
  AVG(DISTINCT scu.capacity) AS avg_capacity
FROM courses_without_prereqs cwp
JOIN section_classroom_usage scu ON scu.course_id = cwp.course_id
GROUP BY cwp.dept_name
ORDER BY cwp.dept_name ASC

rows.pred_sql:
WITH department_course_counts AS (
  SELECT
    c.dept_name AS dept_name,
    COUNT(*) AS dept_course_count
  FROM course c
  GROUP BY c.dept_name
)
SELECT
  c.title,
  c.dept_name,
  d.dept_course_count
FROM course c
LEFT JOIN prereq p
  ON p.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN department_course_counts d
  ON d.dept_name = c.dept_name
WHERE p.course_id IS NULL
ORDER BY c.dept_name ASC, c.title ASC
